verdicts.assertion: Uses a colorblind-safe palette and names it or its source
verdicts.reason: Names the Okabe and Ito colorblind-safe palette and notes the one swap (pink for yellow).

verdicts.assertion: Specifies label text color or contrast for the slices
verdicts.reason: The table gives a label text color for each slice (white on blue, near-black #111111 on the rest) and the checks discuss contrast.

verdicts.assertion: Mentions that color should not be the only way to separate slices
verdicts.reason: It suggests white borders and neighbor lightness differences, but never says color shouldn't be the sole separator or recommends direct labels, patterns or other non-color cues.

verdicts.assertion: Raises that the brand colors may turn into similar grays
verdicts.reason: The answer says the brand colors already land on different grays and stay apart, so it never warns they might print as similar grays. It only hedges that slices 3 and 4 could look close.

verdicts.assertion: Recommends direct labels or patterns in addition to color
verdicts.reason: Print rules say to label each slice directly with its name and value instead of a legend so the chart reads without color.

verdicts.assertion: Provides hex values for four slices
verdicts.reason: The table gives four hex fills: #1F4E79, #DEEBF7, #787878 and #F2A900.
Check #1 is a grayscale check, with a recommended test print on the actual printer and a note that the grays are calculated, not measured.
